analysis.title: Crude Crashes As Blue-nami Sparks Market Chaos; Bullion, Bitcoin, & Bonds Bid
key_insights: Hedges bought ahead of a Democratic sweep were unwound after the result, which pushed volatility lower and drove a delta/gamma-flow rebound in equities from overnight lows. VIX fell back below 17.
Brent fell roughly 10% to a session low of $93.22, its lowest in two months, and WTI fell about 9% to $87-88. Markets read the Democratic sweep as a step toward ending the Iran conflict sooner.
Oil's drop pulled 10Y breakevens to their lowest since August. Yields fell 6-8bps across the curve and the 10Y closed below 5.00%, its lowest close in two months.

Money rotated out of AI capex spenders (semis, neoclouds, optical networking, data-center names) into cash-generating mega-caps. AMZN rose over 8%, AAPL and MSFT rose more than 6% each to record highs, and the Mag7 gained over 3%, its best day since August.

The Broad AI basket fell almost 5% while SPX ex-AI rose over 2%. Neoclouds, optical networking and data-center stocks fell after a Texas gubernatorial winner campaigned for a data-center construction moratorium.
Data-center CDS spreads hit a record high while hyperscaler CDS spreads tightened and IG spreads narrowed.
Energy had its worst day of the year. Refiners VLO and CVR fell about 10%, and upstream names DVN, Kosmos and Baytex fell 6-12%.
US distillate stockpiles fell below 100 million barrels for the first time since 2003, but diesel still fell to near two-month lows with crude.
The dollar had its worst day since early September, gold had its best day since August and closed back above $4,050, and Bitcoin recovered to above $80,000 after a weak overnight start.
Goldman counted 21 equity baskets with moves above 3 sigma, the most since June 5 and the second most in a one-year lookback.

Treasury's refunding statement kept note and bond auction sizes unchanged for the next several quarters and dropped the prior 'at least' qualifier. Dealers read this as leaving open future supply increases.
December rate-hike odds rose modestly despite lower oil. Friday's payrolls print is the next key catalyst for the Fed path.

Post-midterm seasonality was cited by several desks. JPMorgan says SPX has been up a year after every midterm since 1950, averaging about 15%. Over 3, 6, 9 and 12 months it has averaged +5.4%, +11.4%, +12.5% and +14.7%.

market_movers.rationale: Rose over 8% as part of the rotation from AI capex spenders into mega-caps. Goldman said AAPL, MSFT and AMZN made up 65% of the NDX move.
Rose more than 6% to a record high. Investors saw it as a winner from a possible tariff rollback.
Rose more than 6% to a record high, led the rebound with AAPL, and was seen as a beneficiary of tariff rollback hopes.
Fell about 10% as crude dropped on Iran de-escalation hopes.
Fell 6-12% along with upstream energy names as oil dropped on the Democratic sweep.
The combined TSLA/SPCX market cap fell $126BN.

sector_views.rationale: Money rotated from AI capex spenders and semis into hyperscalers and cash-generating mega-caps. Goldman's desk net sold $1.5bn of Info Tech, the 5th straight day of sell skew.
Energy had its worst day of the year as crude fell on the Iran de-escalation read.
Consumer discretionary stocks reached their highest levels since May, and 183 of 185 S&P 1500 members rose.
Homebuilders rose sharply as Treasury yields fell on expectations that divided government would constrain fiscal policy.

macro_indicators.interpretation: A roughly 10% drop to a two-month low as the geopolitical risk premium came out of crude.
Lowest closing level in two months, with yields down 6-8bps across the curve.
First time since 2003. Midwest inventories are the lowest since November 2014.
Best day since August, moving with the weaker dollar.
Recovered after a weak overnight start as the tech rotation accelerated.

crypto_views: Bitcoin was weak overnight on crypto skepticism, then rose back above $80,000 as the tech rotation accelerated. The report says crypto is 'in the crosshairs'.
Gold and crypto were supported by the weaker dollar after yields fell.

trade_ideas.description: Long duration (Treasuries) and long-dated hyperscaler credit risk
trade_ideas.rationale: Goldman IG credit trader Kevin Boova says a slower data-center buildout should be a tailwind for fixed income and that compute scarcity helps hyperscalers.

trade_ideas.description: Buy December $85 and $83 WTI puts (positioning observed in flows, not a recommendation)
trade_ideas.rationale: Bloomberg's Michael Ball notes heavy put interest, which looks like higher-conviction positioning for lower crude.

risk_factors: The tech rebound may not survive overnight trading as Korea opens.
Friday's payrolls could force a repricing of the Fed path if they surprise to the upside.
Data-center CDS spreads are at a record high, which points to funding stress in AI capex.
Further AI regulation or data-center moratoriums under a Democratic majority.
Treasury's refunding wording leaves room for larger auction sizes later.
vol_and_positioning: VIX fell back below 17 as deeply in-the-money protection was sold, which drove delta/gamma flow-driven buying.
Goldman's desk rated activity '6 out of 10' in pockets most affected by the midterms, with long-onlys and hedge funds slightly better to buy on modest numbers.
Goldman's desk net sold $1.5bn of Info Tech, the 5th straight day of sell skew, and sold HC, utilities and REITs. They bought ETFs and hyperscalers.
Crude put volume ran about 1.6x call volume, with heavy interest in December $85 and $83 WTI puts. Brent call skew fell notably (Bloomberg's Michael Ball).
21 Goldman equity baskets had moves above 3 sigma, the most since June 5.
NDX bounced off its 200DMA. SPX moved back above its 100DMA and met support/resistance at its 50DMA.
geopolitical: The Democratic sweep of both chambers of Congress in the US midterms is read as a step toward ending the Iran War sooner.
Trump said he would not escalate in Iran any time soon. GS Hatzius expects Democrats to use fiscal deadlines to try to limit the war.
JD Vance posted blaming Republican losses on the Middle East war, which reinforced the de-escalation read.
The winning Democratic candidate in the Texas governor's race campaigned for a moratorium on new data-center construction.
cross_bank_references: GS Hatzius and DB Saravelos both argue gridlock and a Democratic majority lower the risk premium.
JPMorgan's seasonality view was described as fitting its pre-results expectations.

tension_points.bull_case: Gridlock lowers the risk premium, seasonality is strong (SPX higher 100% of the time 6 months after the past 19 midterms), and Goldman's Boova thinks markets are a buy.
tension_points.bear_case: The rally leans on unwound hedges and rotation, the Broad AI basket fell almost 5%, data-center CDS is at a record high, and 21 Goldman baskets had 3-sigma moves.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A reversal in overnight trading as Korea opens, or an upside payrolls surprise on Friday that reprices the Fed path.

tension_points.bull_case: Compute scarcity lifts pricing for hyperscalers, and slower buildout means less spending and more buybacks.
tension_points.bear_case: Neoclouds, optical networking and data-center stocks sold off, and data-center CDS spreads hit a record high.

theme_stances.key_argument: Compute scarcity lets hyperscalers sell capacity at higher prices, and less capex frees cash for buybacks.
theme_stances.evidence: Goldman described the clear rotation into hyperscalers

theme_stances.key_argument: Gridlock tends to be good for Wall Street, and post-midterm seasonality has been consistently positive.
The Democratic sweep is priced as a reduction in the geopolitical risk premium that kept crude elevated.
